extracted.intended_audience: QHP issuers (FFEs and SBE-FPs), web-brokers and DE partners, State Exchanges, insurers, health policy stakeholders, and public commenters on ACA Exchange Payment Notice rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of regulatory criteria and evaluation metrics from an HHS proposed rule on (1) adjustments to catastrophic plan maximum out-of-pocket (MOOP) and actuarial value considerations and (2) the proposal to discontinue standardized plan options and related display and design requirements for QHPs on the FFEs and SBE-FPs beginning PY2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catastrophic plan MOOP adjustment (130% proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to allow catastrophic plans to have a maximum annual limitation on cost sharing equal to 130 percent of the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing (i.e., raise catastrophic MOOP beyond what Congress specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek comment on whether to finalize 130 percent or a different factor; rationale is to harmonize plan/market outcomes with ACA sections 1302(c)–(e) and preserve catastrophic plan availability without jeopardizing metal-tier framework. If finalized, all catastrophic plans an issuer offers for PY2027 would be required to use the higher annual limitation on cost sharing. Consider phased implementation over multiple plan years to ease impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical actuarial value target for catastrophic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comment on whether HHS should strive for a theoretical AV for catastrophic plans that is higher or lower than 55 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request input on AV target and whether to phase in multiplication factor; consider effects on consumer incentives (especially healthy, non‑subsidized enrollees) and interaction with metal‑tier framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catastrophic plans: 'no benefits until threshold' requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comment on whether to require catastrophic plans to provide no benefits for any plan year (except as provided in §156.155(a)(4),(b),(c)) until an amount equal to 130 percent of the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also solicit alternatives: (a) require at least one catastrophic plan in the same service area to provide no benefits until an amount equal to 100 percent before allowing 130% plans; (b) allow catastrophic plans to provide no benefits until an amount less than 130% but not less than 100%. Consider rounding (130% rounded down to next lowest multiple of $50) and potential impacts on consumers and market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year term requirement for catastrophic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to allow issuers to offer catastrophic plans with a multi-year term and, if finalized, require all catastrophic plans an issuer wishes to offer for PY2027 to use the higher annual limitation on cost sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit comment on operational impacts and interaction with plan offering processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of HHS risk adjustment impacts from catastrophic MOOP changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on whether there would be impacts to HHS risk adjustment as a result of requiring catastrophic plans to provide no benefits until the specified MOOP threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request evidence or analysis on how catastrophic MOOP changes would affect risk adjustment transfers and program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to publish updated MOOP limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the guidance document on the 'Premium Adjustment Percentage, Maximum Annual Limitation on Cost Sharing, Reduced Maximum Annual Limitation on Cost Sharing, and Required Contribution Percentage', or another regulatory vehicle (e.g., Payment Notice), is the appropriate vehicle to release the additional permitted MOOP limitation annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite comment on which venue is preferable for releasing and seeking comment on updated MOOP limitations ahead of each plan year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuation of standardized plan option requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal that, effective PY2027, FFE and SBE-FP QHP issuers in the individual market would no longer be required to offer standardized plan options; remove definition at §155.20, all requirements at §156.201, authority to differentially display at §155.205(b)(1), and corresponding DE pathway requirements at §§155.220(c)(3)(i)(H) and 156.265(b)(3)(iv); cease annual design/publication of these plans in Payment Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not affect State-enacted standardized plan option requirements; issuers may continue offering existing standardized plan options voluntarily, with or without modifications, subject to plan and uniform modification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design principles for standardized plan options
rubrics_metrics.description: When HHS designed standardized plan options previously, it: selected the most popular cost sharing type for each benefit category; selected enrollee-weighted median cost sharing values for each benefit category based on PY2022 cost sharing and enrollment data; modified plans to comply with State cost sharing laws; and decreased AVs to the floor of each AV de minimis range primarily by increasing deductibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These design steps were intended to make standardized options resemble popular QHP offerings and comply with state constraints; commenters may consider these principles when assessing standardized option utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful differentiation requirement for multiple standardized options
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement finalized in 2026: FFE and SBE-FP QHP issuers offering multiple standardized plan options within the same product network type, metal level, and service area must meaningfully differentiate these plans from one another in terms of included benefits, provider networks, included prescription drugs, or a combination (§156.201(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement builds on the historical 'meaningful difference' standard (previously codified at §156.298) intended to prevent duplicative offerings and limit plan proliferation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential display and consumer-facing labeling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Differential display on HealthCare.gov and DE pathways: standardized plan options were visually distinguished as 'easy pricing' plans, including an icon, hover text explaining benefits and distinctions, a 'quick tip', and a filter to view only standardized plan options (§155.205(b)(1), §§155.220(c)(3)(i)(H), 156.265(b)(3)(iv)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for alternate differentiation formats from web brokers or QHP issuers are reviewed based on whether the same or similar level of differentiation and clarity is provided as on HealthCare.gov. Under the proposal, these differential display requirements would be removed, and standardized plans would no longer be visually distinguished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics for evaluating plan proliferation and choice overload
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary metric used: weighted average number of total plans available per enrollee (preferred over unweighted average); also weighted average number of total plans offered per issuer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighting by enrollment gives greater impact to service areas with more enrollees and more closely resembles actual enrollee experience; used to assess choice overload, suboptimal selection risk, and unexpected financial harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uptake and appeal metrics for standardized plan options
rubrics_metrics.description: Use empirical measures such as percent of total enrollment in standardized plan options, percent of total plan offerings that are standardized options, and percent of active plan selections that are standardized options to evaluate consumer appeal and distinguishability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed low uptake (e.g., 20% enrollment in PY2023, 33% in PY2024/2025; active selection rates lower) is cited as evidence that standardized options did not meaningfully appeal to consumers or were hard to distinguish from non-standardized options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-standardized plan option limits and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy tools used: limit of four non-standardized plan options introduced in PY2024, reduced to two in PY2025, and an exceptions process for these limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These limits aimed to reduce plan proliferation but resulted in marginal net reductions and added regulatory complexity and issuer burden (certification applications, portfolio adjustments). Evaluate tradeoffs between limiting choices and imposing burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crosswalk and transition rules when standardized plans discontinued or modified
rubrics_metrics.description: If issuers discontinue existing standardized plan offerings, enrollees would be crosswalked to a different plan per the crosswalk hierarchy at §155.335(j). If issuers continue offering same cost sharing, enrollees auto-reenroll; if issuers modify cost sharing, they remain subject to the definition of 'plan' at §144.103 and uniform modification requirements at §147.106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural requirements govern enrollee transitions and issuer responsibilities when plan offerings change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of literature and context when assessing pricing effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate empirical literature (e.g., 2024 study on 'Simple Choice') cautiously: observed premium reductions in volatile market contexts may not generalize to stable environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS emphasizes that pricing effects from plan standardization may have been transient and context-dependent; commenters should consider market stability and external factors when interpreting such studies.
